core.title: Use the bare artifact name as a contract schema's identity
core.given: You are planning, authoring or editing a contract schema, or a product capability manifest produce/consume entry that references one.
core.when: The schema's identity field is set, changed or present, or a reference to the contract is written.
core.then: Set the contract schema's identity field to the bare artifact identity given by the profile's contract identity shape — with no namespace prefix and no version segment.
prefer: Required: record the contract's version in a separate top-level version field of the schema, never inside the identity field.
Write the product capability manifest produce/consume reference in the profile's contract-reference shape, using exactly the referenced schema's artifact identity as the referenced name.
Keep the identity field stable across versions; express a new version through the separate version field.
avoid: Adding a version suffix to the identity field; it breaks identity stability across versions.
Prefixing the identity field with the profile's forbidden identity prefix.
core.why: Keeping the version out of the identity means the artifact keeps the same identity across versions, so the identity field and contract references always point to one stable artifact.
evidence: Each contract schema's identity field matches the profile's contract identity shape, with no forbidden identity prefix and no version segment.
Each contract schema has a separate top-level version field.
Product capability manifest produce/consume references match the profile's contract-reference shape, and their referenced artifact name equals the referenced schema's identity field.
verification: Scope: contract schemas and product capability manifests wherever the profile locates those plan-artifact kinds; documents that are neither, and manifest edits that do not touch produce/consume contract references, are out of scope.
The invariant applies to the whole schema, not only to edited fields; there are no exceptions (the rule declares none).

The check extracts the identity value, the separate version field and the produce/consume contract references from schemas and manifests; this requires a diff/content observer for those values (the change facts are needs_new_observer in this realization).
Flag any identity value that does not match the profile's contract identity shape, carries a trailing version segment, or starts with the profile's forbidden identity prefix.
Flag contract schemas lacking a separate top-level version field.
Flag produce/consume references whose referenced artifact name differs from the referenced schema's identity field.

Per-rule severity and disposition stay with the realization (the reference sidecar declares none beyond kind: rule, status: active); detector, validator, finding and term ids of this rule are realization details.

product capability manifest with produce/consume entries

fires: A planner writes a new contract schema and sets its identity field.
A planner bumps a contract's version and is tempted to put the version into the identity field.
A planner edits any part of an existing contract schema whose identity is prefixed, versioned or missing, or which lacks a separate version field.
A planner adds or edits a product capability manifest produce/consume entry that references a contract.
doesNotFire: Documents that are neither contract schemas nor product capability manifests (e.g. prose docs, plans without contract references).
Product capability manifest edits that do not touch produce/consume contract references.

neutralityNotes: All concrete identifier syntax is now profile data: the artifact-identity grammar comes from urn.contract ({theme}:{resource}[.{category}]), the forbidden namespace prefix from urn.grammar#forbidden_identity_prefix ('urn:contract:'), the contract-reference shape from urn.grammar#contract_reference_shape (contract:{artifact_name}) and the identity field's concrete name from urn.grammar#contract_identity_field ($id) — moved off idiom.plan_syntax, whose scope is plan constructs, onto urn.grammar, which explicitly covers identity fields and reference shapes. The core keeps the neutral obligations: bare version-independent identity, separate top-level version field (kept as a mandatory 'Required:' prefer), identity stability across versions, and reference equality with the schema's identity. 'Product capability manifest' and 'contract schema' are ATDD structural concepts; the concrete artifact kinds and their locations come from roles.plan_artifact.kinds and roles.plan_artifact.path, and because the neutral activation vocabulary has no path-glob fact kind, activation.facts[2] is carried only as profile data. Worked example and counter-example values stay bunOnly. The sidecar's bookkeeping fields (audit, splitSuggestion, additions, trace) are realization metadata outside the neutral item numbering and are not classified.
